articles.title: Hawley launches investigation into Flock cameras’ massive surveillance program
articles.summary: Sen. Josh Hawley (R-Mo.), the chair of the Senate Judiciary Subcommittee on Crime and Counterterrorism, has launched an investigation into Flock Safety’s national surveillance network and is demanding to know who has access to the personal data of Americans captured on Flock cameras. Hawley wrote in a letter to Flock CEO Garrett Langley that the…
articles.body:
Sen. Josh Hawley (R-Mo.), the chair of the Senate Judiciary Subcommittee on Crime and Counterterrorism, has launched an investigation into Flock Safety’s national surveillance network and is demanding to know who has access to the personal data of Americans captured on Flock cameras.

Hawley wrote in a letter to Flock CEO Garrett Langley that the company has “assembled an unprecedented national surveillance network ” of more than 120,000 cameras across 49 states that conducts 20 billion vehicle scans every month.

“The overwhelming majority of Americans captured in those records did nothing wrong. Instead of serving discrete local investigations, as contemplated by our constitutional processes and safeguards, these camera networks harness artificial intelligence to pool what they capture into a national database that customers can search,” he wrote.

Hawley said this has led to the “abuse and misuse of personal data” due to “the woeful lack of safeguards in these systems.”

He pointed out that in Missouri’s St. Charles County, the police department terminated its contract with Flock after an audit revealed that a civilian employee had run Flock searches for personal reasons unrelated to law enforcement activities.

And he cited a case in Milwaukee, where prosecutors charged a police officer who allegedly searched his girlfriend’s license plate number 124 times and her former boyfriend’s plate 55 times.

Flock’s safeguards didn’t catch the misconduct of the Milwaukee officer, who was caught after the former boyfriend searched his own plate on haveibeenflocked.com and discovered it had been searched for on numerous occasions.

Hawley said the surveillance notifications have also resulted in mistaken arrests, such as that of a Florida woman who spent 13 days in jail and faced multiple felony counts after investigators mistakenly arrested her based on a search of Flock’s network.

“Errors and false positives add insult to injury,” Hawley wrote.

He cited one California police department that found that 71 percent of its Flock alerts “were wrong” and noted the Los Angeles Police Department ended its Flock contract after an audit showed its officers had stopped 161 vehicles incorrectly flagged as stolen.

Hawley said Americans want to know who has access to their personal data collected on Flock’s network and has asked the company to provide all relevant documents and information no later than Sept. 8.

“Once cameras collect driver data, uncertainty abounds in how your company and its customers can sell or use data,” Hawley wrote, adding that the company’s $8.3 billion valuation creates “enormous pressure to find new commercial applications.”

Hawley said he wants law enforcement to have the tools it needs to catch criminal offenders but argued that “Americans do not surrender their privacy rights when they drive to work, drop their kids off at school or go to church.”

articles.title: Dem senator turns ‘leader of the free world’ title on its head with Zelenskyy remarks
articles.summary: Chris Coons declared Volodymyr Zelenskyy is now the free world's primary leader, igniting fierce backlash from the White House and conservatives.
articles.body: Delaware Sen. Chris Coons is facing backlash after declaring that the United States is "no longer" the leader of the free world and pointing instead to Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy as the national leader putting his country "on the line for freedom." "I would say we are no longer the leaders of the free world. In fact, if anything, Volodymyr Zelenskyy is the primary national leader who is putting his country’s men and women on the line for freedom," Coons said during a town hall earlier this month. "We need to earn our place back as leader in the free world in the future." Coons’ remarks underscore his long-running alignment with Kyiv at a moment when President Donald Trump is pressing for an end to the war and putting a renewed emphasis on American power and national pride. TRUMP HAILS AMERICA AS 'MOST EXCEPTIONAL NATION EVER TO EXIST' IN MOUNT RUSHMORE SPEECH The Delaware Democrat has been one of Congress’ more outspoken supporters of Ukraine, repeatedly backing military aid, tougher sanctions on Russia and continued U.S. engagement with Zelenskyy’s government. Coons spoke with Dover, Delaware, Councilman Andre Boggerty alongside Rep. Sarah McBride in a virtual town hall Tuesday hosted by the Kent County Democratic Committee focused on local issues. Coons has been a vocal advocate for sustained U.S. support for Ukraine since Russia launched its full-scale invasion in 2022, repeatedly pressing for military assistance and tougher sanctions on Moscow. Coons visited Kyiv in 2022 to meet with Zelenskyy and visited Odesa with Senate Foreign Relations Committee members in February to reiterate "the ironclad, bipartisan support" for Ukraine, according to a press release. Nick Adams, special presidential envoy for American tourism, exceptionalism and values, told Fox News Digital Coons' comments are "the essence of America last." "The United States is today, has been since 1776, and with God's grace, always will be the leader of the free world. To suggest otherwise is to ignore our Constitution and the bloodshed by our heroes who made sure that our Declaration of Independence would not just be a theoretical document but the beginning of a new era in the history of humanity," Adams said. Adams added that no other nation can hold a candle to America, pointing to its constitutional freedoms, founding principles of liberty and belief that natural rights transcend government authority. WORLD LEADERS, DIGNITARIES PAY TRIBUTE TO AMERICA ON HISTORIC 250TH BIRTHDAY "To say otherwise is to reveal an unbelievable ignorance as to what our nation is, where we came from and how our destiny will always be shaped by the principles of life, liberty and the pursuit of happiness," Adams added. Conservative critics seized on Coons' remarks, accusing him of being "anti-American." "Wow! This is truly sick behavior. Sen. Chris Coons — a Democrat who nobody has ever heard of, but nonetheless a U.S. Senator — says the U.S. is ‘no longer the leaders of the free world’ because ‘Volodymyr Zelenskyy is the primary national leader,’" the White House’s Rapid Response account wrote on X. "Imagine asserting this. What an absolute clown," one user wrote. "Chris Coons has always been an anti-American fraud. He’s a total coward," another person said. ZELENSKYY PRESSURES US AND EUROPE FOR MORE 'AIR DEFENSE' ASSISTANCE AMID ONGOING WAR WITH RUSSIA "What an embarrassment he is — Ukraine hasn’t held elections since 2019," a user commented. The Russia-Ukraine war has dragged on for more than four years, with Kyiv holding off a larger Russian force while facing manpower shortages and relying heavily on continued Western weapons. Coons' office did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's press inquiry.

articles.title: ICE detainment reach second-term high for Trump administration: Report
articles.summary: Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) detained almost 50,000 people in July, marking its highest monthly arrest total during President Trump’s second term, newly released data shows. According to numbers published in the Deportation Data Project — a joint project conducted by the University of California, Berkeley and University of California, Los Angeles — ICE arrested…
articles.body:
Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) detained almost 50,000 people in July, marking its highest monthly arrest total during President Trump’s second term, newly released data shows.

According to numbers published in the Deportation Data Project — a joint project conducted by the University of California, Berkeley and University of California, Los Angeles — ICE arrested 49,571 people in July 2026. A Monday Associated Press analysis noted that the figure marked a surge in detainments, jumping by 15 percent from the month prior.

For the majority of 2026, detention numbers stagnated around the lower 30,000 range. Detainments in July jumped by 70 percent from when this plateau began in February.

Since the Trump administration’s February immigration crackdown in Minnesota, called Operation Metro Surge , ICE and Customs and Border Protection have expanded their enforcement across the country. The agencies have also invested heavily in their officers as President Trump rolls back deportation protections for several migrant groups.

Cristy Maryori Villafranca-Trejo, the wife of Army Sgt. Hedar Leonel Turcios Juarez, was deported Monday — marking the seventh spouse or parent of an active-duty military member who was removed from the country.

“I don’t know if I will be able to continue with this,” Turcios Juarez told the AP. “I have to make a plan to make sure I can still fulfill my military responsibilities — but also take care of my family.”

Navy sailor Joshua Aviles — currently serving aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln , which earlier this month faced scrutiny for declining living conditions — similarly reported that his father had been detained by ICE. After Aviles’s social media pleas, his father was released from custody Wednesday.

“I don’t know how I can mentally continue working 12+ hour days knowing that my dad is somewhere, possibly being treated like a criminal,” the sailor wrote in his initial post.

ICE also deported more than 160 immigrants to Haiti last week, acting on a June Supreme Court ruling that allowed the Trump administration to end Temporary Protected Status for around 330,000 Haitians and more than 6,000 Syrians.

But polls suggest public approval of ICE’s expanded efforts is dwindling. In early August, the AP and NORC Center for Public Affairs Research found that Americans’ approval of Trump’s handling of immigration had dropped by 10 percentage points since the start of his second term, reaching a 58 percent disapproval rate.

An earlier New York Times/Siena poll , published in January, found that nearly half of respondents said they believed Trump had “ gone too far ” in restricting legal immigration.

articles.title: 2028 Dem hopeful slaps Trump admin with lawsuit over mail-in-voting after major SCOTUS victory
articles.summary: Pennsylvania Gov. Josh Shapiro joins 23 states suing USPS over Trump-backed mail-ballot rule, arguing Congress—not the president or Postal Service—sets federal election rules.
articles.body: With the November midterms approaching, Pennsylvania Gov. Josh Shapiro is joining attorneys general from 23 states and Washington, D.C., in suing the U.S. Postal Service (USPS) over a Trump-backed mail-ballot rule that would impose new federal requirements on how states prepare and send mail ballots. "I’m suing the Trump Administration to stop their unconstitutional attempt to change the rules and restrict mail-in voting. I’ll remind the President of my track record going up against him in court — and winning — to protect Pennsylvania’s free, fair, safe, and secure elections. I’m prepared to do so again," Shapiro wrote on X. "Nothing about voting by mail has changed here in Pennsylvania. You can still vote safely and securely by mail." "While Donald Trump may try to inject chaos into our elections, the Constitution is clear: the authority to set election rules belongs to the states — not the federal government," he continued. The two-dozen-state coalition returned to court two days after the Supreme Court stayed an earlier injunction issued by a Massachusetts federal judge against key parts of Trump’s mail-voting executive order, finding the states’ initial challenge premature because USPS had not yet issued a final rule when they filed suit. TRUMP SCORES SUPREME COURT WIN ON MAIL-IN VOTING RESTRICTIONS BEFORE MIDTERMS "The Supreme Court ruling was a major win for the security of American elections. Radical Democrats continue to oppose commonsense measures that protect the security of mail-in ballots and ensure only Americans are electing American leaders," White House spokeswoman Lauren Bis said in a statement to Fox News Digital. "The Trump Administration will continue to lawfully enact the agenda President Trump was elected on – which includes the safety and security of our elections." At issue is USPS’s newly finalized "Ballot Mail for Federal Elections" rule, which went into effect last week and was published Wednesday. It would require state and local election officials to submit information on intended mail-ballot recipients to a USPS portal, where the agency would compile state-specific lists of enrolled mail voters. It would also require certain mail-in ballot design requirements, such as trackable barcodes, and require officials to submit ballot-envelope designs to USPS for pre-approval. In their 53-page complaint, the states argue that the rule improperly gives USPS a new role in running elections, forcing election officials to adopt new procedures, share ballot-recipient information and potentially replace already-purchased envelopes as the midterms draw closer. They also argue that Congress, not the president or Postal Service, has the authority to alter election rules, and that USPS skipped a review process for major nationwide changes to postal services or operations. NEWSOM PROMISES NEW LEGAL FIGHT AFTER TRUMP GETS SUPREME COURT VICTORY ON MAIL-IN VOTING The coalition is asking the court to block the rule while the lawsuit proceeds and ultimately throw it out, arguing that their new challenge answers the Supreme Court’s timing concern. A separate Massachusetts injunction had temporarily blocked USPS from putting the requirements in place for the November midterms, but the judge lifted that order Wednesday following the Supreme Court’s ruling. "This Court held that 'no law enacted by Congress delegates authority to control mail-in voting to USPS,' and that the President’s directives to USPS were ultra vires," the states write in their complaint. "The Supreme Court subsequently stayed the injunction—not because Plaintiff States’ claims lacked merit, but because the States 'lack[ed] standing to bring' their claims as to the [Executive Order] ... As the Court explained, USPS had not yet implemented the EO, but if USPS ultimately adopts a final rule that 'harms the States, they may challenge that rule.' USPS then published its final rule two days later." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP USPS did not respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment in time for publication.

articles.title: America’s heartland comes face-to-face with 9/11 history as 25th anniversary nears
articles.summary: The "Steel Across America" tour brought a 16,900-pound South Tower beam to Cincinnati as Scott Nokes, a double amputee veteran, shared his story.
articles.body: A nearly 17,000-pound piece of steel from the World Trade Center’s South Tower made its way to Cincinnati, giving people hundreds of miles from Ground Zero a rare chance to stand face-to-face with a piece of 9/11 history. "Never Forgetting the sacrifice and bravery of our nation’s heroes, as well as our lost loved ones, is a generational promise that every American can help keep," Tunnel to Towers Foundation chairman and CEO Frank Siller told Fox News Digital. The 21-foot steel beam is making its way across the country as part of Tunnel to Towers’ "Steel Across America" tour, a traveling memorial marking 25 years since the Sept. 11 terrorist attacks. Former Marine infantryman Scott Nokes, a Tunnel to Towers ambassador and employee, joined local firefighters, FDNY members, veterans, first responders and community members in bringing the beam to the Cincinnati Fire Museum on Saturday. TUNNEL TO TOWERS ANNOUNCES 'STEEL ACROSS AMERICA' TOUR TO MARK 25 YEARS SINCE 9/11 ATTACKS "I know firsthand what it means to have the Tunnel to Towers Foundation show up for you when you need it most," said Nokes at the event. "This foundation changes lives. It changed mine. When I stand before this steel and think about the men and women we lost on September 11, I feel an obligation to make sure their story keeps being told. I am honored to be here, today, as part of this journey." MASSIVE PIECE OF 9/11 HISTORY MAKES STUNNING 10,500-MILE JOURNEY ACROSS AMERICA New Jersey native Nokes was deployed twice to Afghanistan before leaving the service to pursue firefighting. In 2016, he went into septic shock, and life-saving treatment left him a double below-the-knee amputee and legally blind. Through Tunnel to Towers’ Smart Home Program, Nokes received a custom, mortgage-free smart home in December 2019 designed to help him live more independently.In addition to working and representing T2T, Nokes mentors for Neptune Emergency Services. The stop gave community members, first responders, veterans and residents the chance to see the artifact in person during a ceremony featuring a color guard, bagpipes, the national anthem, a blessing of the beam, a moment of silence, remarks from fire and city leaders, and a Steel Flag presentation. AS AMERICAN PRIDE HITS A 25-YEAR LOW, A NEW 9/11 EDUCATION PLATFORM URGES THE NATION TO NEVER FORGET The steel beam has served as a traveling memorial to the victims and first responders of 9/11, offering pop-up events across 21 different states leading up to the anniversary of the tragic day. After Cincinnati, the tour heads into its final stretch, with stops scheduled at the U.S. Military Academy at West Point on Sept. 1, the Massachusetts Fallen Heroes Memorial in Boston on Sept. 3 and the White House on Sept. 8 before returning to New York City. The foundation is honoring the 343 FDNY firefighters who died on 9/11 by delivering 343 mortgage-free homes this year.

articles.title: Georgia mail carrier sentenced after stealing $1M in checks: DOJ
articles.summary: McAfee pleaded guilty to possession of stolen mail on May 14, 2026, and was sentenced this week.
articles.body:
( NewsNation ) — A former U.S. Postal Service (USPS) mail carrier in Georgia was sentenced to two years in federal prison for stealing items worth more than $1 million.

Melissa McAfee, 44, delivered packages in the Smyrna area, near Atlanta, from August 2022 to September 2024, the U.S. Department of Justice said in a release . Though the exact timeline remains unclear, the USPS Office of Inspector General launched an investigation after customers complained about stolen mail on her route.

During the investigation, USPS-OIG received surveillance footage showing McAfee was responsible for the thefts, according to the release. Postal Service agents also executed a search warrant at her home and found envelopes containing stolen mail, 145 checks and 37 gift cards. Overall, they determined she stole 171 checks worth more than $1,035,000.

McAfee pleaded guilty to possession of stolen mail on May 14, 2026, and was sentenced this week to two years in prison followed by two years of supervised release. She was also ordered to pay an undisclosed amount in restitution.

“Today’s sentencing sends a strong message to anyone who thinks mail theft and check fraud will go unpunished,” Jonathan Ulrich, Special Agent in Charge of the U.S. Postal Service Office of Inspector General, said.

“Our special agents, along with our federal and local law enforcement partners, will aggressively investigate these federal crimes,” he added.

In May, the DOJ announced two former postal carriers, a former Georgia bank manager and a “convicted felon” face federal charges in an alleged multimillion-dollar mail theft and bank fraud scheme.

NewsNation’s Sean Noone contributed to this report.

articles.title: GOP nominee for Maine governor calls for ICE agents at state polling places
articles.summary: PORTLAND, Maine — Maine’s Republican nominee for governor recently told a crowd of supporters that he would ask a top Department of Homeland Security official to send U.S.
articles.body: PORTLAND, Maine — Maine’s Republican nominee for governor recently told a crowd of supporters that he would ask a top Department of Homeland Security official to send U.S. Marshals and Immigration and Customs Enforcement agents to polling places in the state for this fall’s midterm elections, according to audio obtained by The Associated Press. During an Aug. 20 event in Arundel, Bobby Charles told a group of supporters that he would ask Tom Homan, the White House border czar, to send federal agents to polling places in the weeks before Election Day. The audio was first reported by the Bangor Daily News. “Here’s my secret,” Charles told members of a Maine Young Republicans chapter. “I have a friend named Tom Homan. Tom and I used to get on Fox all the time together. Tom’s an awesome guy.” “I’m going to ask Tom, I’m going to actually — three or four weeks before the election, maybe three — I’m going to make an appeal for ICE and Marshals to be at our voting booths,” Charles said, according to the audio. On Wednesday, he explained his comments by saying state and local authorities who manage elections should have an open line of communication with federal authorities if needed to “prevent violence at a voting place, in order to prevent intimidation at a voting place and in order to prevent illegality at a voting place.” He said his point was that Maine authorities should do everything legally possible to prevent illegal voting in the state. “Everybody who is legally entitled to vote should be free from any intimidation and should be able to vote,” he said in a statement released by his campaign. “Anybody who is not legally entitled to vote should not be voting.” Charles’ comments come as President Donald Trump continues to sow doubt about the security of elections in the U.S. elections and takes unprecedented measures to intervene in election administration. The Constitution gives states, and sometimes Congress, the authority to set election rules but grants no such power to the president. A central part of his attacks is to claim widespread fraud through voting by noncitizens. But those claims are vastly overstated. Voting by noncitizens is exceptionally rare and is punishable as a felony, with deportation as one potential penalty. Nevertheless, Trump has been pushing Congress to pass a bill that would require voters to show documentary proof of citizenship to vote in the upcoming midterms and signed an executive order directing the Postal Service to send mail ballots only to those on an approved list of verified voters. When reached for comment on Wednesday, DHS did not address whether department officials had held or planned to hold conversations with political campaigns about election security. DHS officials have previously said they do not have plans to send ICE agents to polling places. “Elections exist for the American people, not illegal aliens, to choose their leaders,” a Homeland Security spokesperson said in a statement to the AP. Democratic state officials have been concerned about the possibility of immigration agents showing up near polling places on Election Day or during early voting. In February, a DHS official told a group of secretaries of state that “any suggestion that ICE will be present at any polling location is simply not true,” according to several secretaries who were part of the conversation. Maine Secretary of State Shenna Bellows, a Democrat, said ICE agents are prohibited by law from being at polling places. Bellows ran for governor this year but lost the Democratic primary. “The political rhetoric coming from Mr. Charles is just politics, but it won’t change the laws or the Constitution,” Bellows said. The Maine Democratic Party also criticized Charles’ comments and described his plan as likely illegal. The party also criticized the timing of the comments as the state is continuing to wrestle with the killing of Biddeford resident Johan Sebastián Durán Guerrero by an ICE officer earlier this summer. The comments expose Charles as a “MAGA extremist” who will do Trump’s bidding, said Maine Democratic Party Executive Director Devon Murphy-Anderson. “His plan to ask Trump’s border czar to send ICE agents to Maine polling places just weeks before Election Day is not only deeply alarming — it is likely illegal,” Murphy-Anderson said. Federal law prohibits the military and federal agencies from putting troops or armed officers near polling sites, according to the Brennan Center. The White House has dismissed concerns that federal agents would interfere with elections and noted that there was no disruption to the election process in last year’s elections, when Democrats performed well. Charles is an attorney who served as U.S. assistant secretary of state under President George W. Bush. He will face Democrat Hannah Pingree, the former speaker of the Maine House of Representatives, in November.

articles.title: Louisiana governor ‘not concerned’ about environmental impact of Gulf Coast SpaceX facility
articles.summary: Louisiana Gov. articles.body:
Louisiana Gov. Jeff Landry (R) on Wednesday morning brushed aside fears about possible negative environmental impacts from SpaceX’s planned $100 billion launch facility in the state.

He told CBS News on Wednesday that he was “not concerned about the environmental impact” of this new spaceport, which will be constructed along the Gulf Coast on a former Exxon property in Vermilion Parish, La.

“What I am concerned about is the lack of economic opportunity on the coast that continues to basically rob us of opportunities to rebuild our coast,” the governor said.

The spaceport will be the company’s fourth and largest launch site, and it will serve as the main facility for Starship, SpaceX’s in-development reusable rocket launch system.

SpaceX got into hot water over its operations at its first launch site in Boca Chica, Texas.

In 2024, the Texas Commission on Environmental Quality found that the company violated environmental regulations by repeatedly releasing pollutants into nearby bodies of water.

This followed an earlier warning by the Environmental Protection Agency Region 6 office, which oversees Texas, that SpaceX violated the Clean Water Act with these actions.

Elon Musk’s company said in a statement that it was committed to working with federal and state agencies and conservation groups “to protect shoreline, restore wetlands, and support the wildlife and recreation that depend on them” in Louisiana.

Musk thanked state partners for their support of this new facility in a statement shared by the Louisiana Economic Development (LED) on Tuesday.

“SpaceX was founded to bring about a future where humans are out exploring amongst the stars, which will only be possible when we make going to space as routine as flying on an airplane,” Musk said. “Starbase, Louisiana will unlock that future.

“Thank you Governor Landry and the people of Louisiana for joining us on this journey, and for their help in the years ahead as we work together to build one of the most inspirational places on the planet,” he continued.

The LED estimated the facility will generate over 11,000 new job opportunities in the area, including around 3,000 direct jobs and over 8,000 indirect jobs.

Construction on this project is anticipated to begin next year with the first launch expected as soon as 2029, according to LED’s announcement.

Landry called this new partnership with SpaceX “the greatest marriage that Louisiana has ever had” in his interview with CBS.

“It’s a great partnership. We are not concerned about those issues,” he said, referring again to the environmental concerns.
